expectations.text: Output produces an execution-ready or launch-ready experiment brief (no critical missing fields blocking launch)
expectations.evidence: Launch Readiness Checklist shows all required fields completed with checkmarks. Plan status explicitly states 'Execution-ready. No critical fields missing. Proceed to implementation handoff.'

expectations.text: Output includes all required structural sections: hypothesis, variants (control + test), target audience with eligibility criteria, primary metric, secondary metrics, guardrails, success threshold, stopping logic, and decision rules
expectations.evidence: All sections present: Hypothesis (paragraph explaining logic), Variants (Control and Test clearly separated), Target Audience & Eligibility (includes 7+ day requirement), Metrics (primary, secondary, guardrails each defined), Success Threshold (≥+10% relative, 95% confidence), Stopping Logic (3 weeks, emergency conditions specified), and Success/Neutral/Failure Outcomes with explicit actions for each.

expectations.text: Output correctly captures the eligibility requirement (≥7 days of activity history required for smart-send model)
expectations.evidence: Eligibility criteria section states: 'Must have at least 7 days of app activity history (required for the smart send time model to generate accurate predictions)'. Also reinforced in Target Audience section with clear rationale.

expectations.text: Output includes at least one operational or validity risk specific to this test (e.g., novelty effect, model accuracy dependency, delivery timing variance, or exposure bias from users with no history)
expectations.evidence: Five specific risks identified in 'Operational & Validity Risks' section: (1) Model accuracy dependency with fallback mitigation, (2) Novelty effect with decay monitoring, (3) Delivery timing variance by time zone/device, (4) Selection bias from 7+ day eligibility rule, (5) External time-based confounds. Each includes mitigation strategy.

expectations.text: Output defines distinct outcomes and follow-on actions for success, partial result (5–9% uplift), and failure
expectations.evidence: Success/Neutral/Failure section defines three distinct branches: Success (roll out, sunset 10am, monitor post-launch), Neutral/Partial (5-9% uplift: do not roll out, refine model, retest in 4-6 weeks), Failure (do not roll out, investigate root cause, explore alternative levers). Each outcome has distinct action pathway.
